Ta có $y' = (2x + 1)e^{-x} - (x^2 + x + 1)e^{-x} = (x - x^2)e^{-x}$.\\
		$y' = 0 \Leftrightarrow (x - x^2)e^{-x} = 0 \Leftrightarrow \left[\begin{array}{l} x = 0 \\ x = 1 \notin [-1; 0] \end{array}\right.$\\
		$y(0) = 1$; $y(-1) = e \Rightarrow \min\limits_{[-1; 0]} y = 1; \max\limits_{[-1; 0]} y = e \Rightarrow \min\limits_{[-1; 0]} y + \max\limits_{[-1; 0]} y = 1 + e \approx 3,7$.
